title: Sound Design to Technical Bridge Schema
description: Schema for bridge entries that translate subjective sound design descriptors to DSP parameters

category.description: Descriptor category for grouping related mappings

descriptor.description: The subjective sound design term being translated

parameter.description: DSP parameter name (must match APVTS parameter ID)

typical_default.description: Suggested default value within the range

parameters.description: Array of parameter mappings that create this sound characteristic

confidence.description: How confident we are in this mapping (0.0 = uncertain, 1.0 = proven)

why.description: Human-readable rationale for the overall mapping

anti_patterns.description: Common mistakes when trying to achieve this sound

related_descriptors.description: Other descriptors that often combine with this one

example_plugins.description: Real plugins that exemplify this sound

user_feedback.description: History of user feedback refining this entry

parameters.why: Reduced high frequencies (lower cutoff) creates warmth by rolling off harsh upper harmonics
Subtle resonance adds character without being harsh
Soft saturation adds harmonic content that psychoacoustically reads as 'warmth'

examples.why: Warmth comes from reduced high frequencies (lower cutoff), subtle resonance for character, and soft saturation that adds pleasing harmonics without harshness.

anti_patterns.reason: Creates nasal, boxy sound rather than warmth

anti_patterns.avoid: Adding warmth through EQ boost instead of filter reduction
anti_patterns.reason: Often adds noise and unmusical resonance; subtractive approach is cleaner

example_plugins.name: u-he Diva
example_plugins.how_used: Low-pass filter with gentle slope + subtle drive

parameters.why: Asymmetric delay times create rhythmic complexity and movement
High feedback creates evolving, self-generating textures
Pitch modulation creates detuning and warbling
Slow modulation creates evolving rather than static repeats
Filtered repeats create darkening echo decay

examples.why: Psychedelic sound design relies on time-based effects (delay, reverb) with high feedback, pitch modulation for warbling/detuning, and filtering that darkens repeats over time.

anti_patterns.reason: Creates static stereo effect without the evolving quality
